about: Question set for the accuracy test of T-72. `result` is the position of the result in the replay; every format of it is given whole, so a question is answered from one format at a time. `answer` is worked out from the raw data. D is today's text with the dictionary in force (its legend first); B and C need `legend`; signatures over 80 characters are clipped in B and C, and no question asks for one.
legend: Every tool takes `format: "compact"` (the default, "text", is unchanged): the same data in a third fewer characters. A compact result starts with `~B` (or `~J` and the JSON of the whole result). `key: value` is a field; a value starting `{` or `[` is JSON; `note: ~I` is the usual "Index incomplete: N of M files are not scanned yet" note built from `index`; `~1` is the hint that searched files are not in the graph yet, `~2` the caveat that `unused` is a candidate list, not proof. `# key f1 f2..` starts function records with those fields; `>dir/` names the directory of the files below it, ` file` a file, `  name#hash<TAB>k=v..` a function in it. THE FUNCTION ID for `source_get` or `deps_get` is the directory and file of its group, `::`, then `name#hash`: `src/a/b.py::name#hash`. Unwritten fields have their default (status="PENDING" possibly_stale=false has_contract=false only_test_callers=false relation="calls" confidence="EXTRACTED"; function_name is the last part of the name). Keys: s=signature st=status p=possibly_stale c=has_contract d=depth r=relation cf=confidence n=function_name o=only_test_callers. A signature past 80 characters ends with `…` (`source_get` has it whole). `^ hits`: under a file, `line<TAB>function<TAB>text` (`=` the row above's function, empty none, `!id` another file's). `% blocks`: `@a-b<TAB>matched lines<TAB>functions`, then lines a..b each led by `:` (matched) or `-`. `& owners`: `*Owner<TAB>count`, files, functions, then `line<TAB>kind<TAB>site<TAB>source`. `= key f1 f2..`: other lists of records, one `|cell<TAB>cell` row each (`~` a field the row lacks); a `<TAB>f=v` after a field list gives every row that value; `{ key` .. `}` holds the lists of a field; in a record `!k` means it has no `k`, and `f[a,b]` in the field list means rows of three spaces and the cells a,b follow each record. A result that does not start with `~B` is the plain text form (sent when it is the shorter). `source_get` is never compacted.
